festivals: Aadi Thabasu / Aadithapasu (July-Aug; flagship festival commemorating Shiva's appearance as Sankaranarayanar)

history.dynasty: Pandya (attributed to Ugra Pandiyan per legend)
history.period: 900+ years old (legend dates the founding to Ugra Pandiyan)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV lists the town as Tiruchendur, which is WRONG. The famous Sankaranainar Kovil - the Sankara Narayanar Temple of the combined Hari-Hara deity - is at SANKARANKOVIL in Tenkasi district, roughly 90-100 km from Tiruchendur; the town itself is named after this temple. It enshrines Sankaranarayanar, half Shiva and half Vishnu, alongside Sankareswarar and Gomathi Amman, and is sacred to both Saivites and devotees who see Shiva and Vishnu as one (Sri Vaishnavites who worship Vishnu alone reject it). The 4.5-acre complex has an imposing 135-ft nine-tier rajagopuram. Legend: king Ugra Pandiyan built the temple where a lingam was found beside a snake pit; Gomathi Amman's nine-day penance at Pungavanakshetram won her the vision of Hari and Hara as one form, commemorated in the Adi Thabasu festival; the Nagachunai tank was dug by serpent kings. The puttumann (ant-hill sand) from the temple is believed to cure diseases. DATE FLAG: Wikipedia's legend says Ugra Pandiyan founded it in '900 BC', while the TNUIFSL city-corporate plan describes a 900-year-old temple - the 900 BC date is legendary, not documented history.

name: Sankaranainar Kovil
town_description: Town in Tenkasi district named for the Sankaranarayanar temple at its heart; known for the Adi Thabasu festival, the Chithirai car festival, and the healing puttumann (ant-hill sand). Earlier called Sankaranayinarkoil.

travel.road: Buses from Madurai (~75 km), Tirunelveli (~50 km) and Tenkasi (~50 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Adi Thabasu (Jul-Aug) is the flagship festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00 PM-9:00 PM daily
